meta.method: Web search verification of 4 Remarkability Ingredients per creator. Only entries with confidence < 85 or corrections needed are included.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. He did reject individual therapy as the default and built Imago around the idea that romantic conflict is a growth opportunity tied to childhood wounds. Well documented.

twoWorlds.notes: The file says 'theologian-turned-psychologist' which is correct (PhD in Psychology and Religion from U of Chicago, ordained Baptist minister). However, calling it 'Academic developmental psychology meets practical couples therapy' undersells the theology angle. His actual two worlds are THEOLOGY + PSYCHOLOGY — he was an ordained minister who got a PhD in psychology and religion. The 'object relations theory' mention is fine but the framing misses the theological root.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Theologian and ordained Baptist minister meets developmental psychology and attachment theory. He has a PhD in Psychology and Religion from the University of Chicago and was a professor at Southern Methodist University, bringing dense attachment theory into a structured couples dialogue process that regular people could actually use.

stupidSimplicity.notes: This is a good compression of his core thesis. Verified through multiple sources.

remarkableResult.notes: Multiple errors: (1) The book has sold over 4 million copies across ALL his books with Helen LaKelly Hunt, not 4 million for this one book alone. (2) It was NOT an 'Oprah Book Club selection' — Oprah featured him 17 times on her show and recommended it, but it was not an official Oprah Book Club pick. (3) The file says '2,000 certified Imago therapists in 53 countries' — sources vary: 2,000-2,500 therapists in 35-62 countries depending on the date. The most recent figure is 2,500+ therapists in 53+ countries.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Together with Helen LaKelly Hunt, their books have sold over 4 million copies. 'Getting the Love You Want' was featured on 17 episodes of the Oprah Winfrey Show. Imago Relationship Therapy became a global movement with over 2,500 certified Imago therapists in 53+ countries. The Imago dialogue process is now taught in graduate programs worldwide.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. Her emphasis on going slowly, doing less, and letting the body discharge at its own pace is well documented. She explicitly contrasts with exposure therapy and talk therapy.

twoWorlds.notes: She has a Master's in Biomedical and Health Science (not just 'biomedical science'). The Feldenkrais training is confirmed (she studied under Moshe Feldenkrais's methods). Peter Levine and Kathy Kain training confirmed. However, calling her a 'musician and recording engineer' would be wrong — that's Jonathan Goldman. Her two worlds description is mostly accurate but should specify 'Master's in Biomedical and Health Science' not just 'biomedical science'.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Biomedical and health science (Master's degree) and Feldenkrais somatic education meets Peter Levine's Somatic Experiencing and Kathy Kain's developmental trauma work. She brings a rigorous biological understanding of the autonomic nervous system to trauma healing.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Good compression of her core message.

remarkableResult.notes: The file says 'millions of views' on YouTube and 'thousands of students globally.' Web sources say her programs have reached 'over 27,000 people in over 90 countries' — much more specific and impressive than 'thousands.' YouTube views claim of 'millions' is plausible but not specifically verified. She was the FIRST person in the Somatic Experiencing/Feldenkrais worlds to offer a full online course — that's a notable claim worth including.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: First professional in the Somatic Experiencing and Feldenkrais worlds to offer a full online self-healing course. Her programs have reached over 27,000 people in over 90 countries. Her YouTube channel has become one of the leading sources of nervous system education online.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. The idea that yoga was solo and individual, and he made it about partner trust, is well documented.

twoWorlds.notes: Verified. He was a competitive Sports Acrobatics athlete (represented the US at age 16 at the 1991 World Championships in Beijing), combined with yoga and Thai massage. The file says 'competitive acrobat' which is correct.

remarkableResult.notes: The file says AcroYoga is 'practiced in 100+ countries with thousands of certified teachers.' Web sources say 1,500+ certified teachers in 55-60+ countries (not 100+), supporting over a million participants. The '100+ countries' claim is inflated; the official AcroYoga.org site says 60+ countries.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Co-founded AcroYoga (with Jenny Sauer-Klein), which grew from informal park jams to a global movement with over 1,500 certified teachers in 60+ countries and over a million participants worldwide. AcroYoga is now recognized as its own distinct discipline alongside traditional yoga styles.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. He filled arenas with mass meditation. Well documented.

twoWorlds.notes: The file says 'Cantora Records' which is correct. However, calling it just 'music industry founder' understates it — he co-founded Cantora Records with Will Griggs (and Nick Panama), and they signed MGMT. Also, 'concert production' framing is good but he was more of a label/management guy than a concert producer.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Co-founder of Cantora Records (the label that signed MGMT) meets mass meditation events. Brought music industry production values, event curation, and cultural cool to contemplative practice.

remarkableResult.notes: Several issues: (1) '23 people' start is verified (December 2014 Medi Club). (2) Madison Square Garden and World Trade Center rooftop are verified venues. (3) However, the 'Oprah and Deepak partnerships' is slightly misleading — he toured with Oprah on her 2020 Vision Tour and did global broadcasts with Deepak, but these were separate engagements, not a joint 'Oprah and Deepak partnership.' (4) Timeline claim of '3 years' from 23 people to MSG is roughly correct (2014 to ~2017). (5) He was also invited on Oprah's 2020 tour with WW, speaking at 15,000+ person arenas.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: 23 people in December 2014 to sold-out meditations at Madison Square Garden, the World Trade Center rooftop, and the American Museum of Natural History within 3 years. Toured with Oprah Winfrey on her 2020 Vision arena tour and led global meditation broadcasts with Deepak Chopra.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. He derived Anusara from Iyengar yoga and reintroduced Tantric/Hindu spirituality with a heart-opening, celebratory philosophy.

twoWorlds.notes: Verified. Iyengar alignment meets Tantric philosophy is well documented.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Good compression of his 'Open to Grace' philosophy.

remarkableResult.notes: The file says '100,000+ students in 70 countries.' Web sources say approximately 500,000-600,000 practitioners in 70 countries with ~1,500 teachers at peak. The student number is significantly understated. Also, the 'Wiccan sex coven' detail is verified (The Blazing Solar Flames). The word 'allegations' undersells it — multiple sources confirm the coven existed.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Built Anusara into one of the fastest-growing yoga styles in the world with approximately 1,500 certified teachers and 500,000-600,000 practitioners in 70 countries at its peak around 2010-2012. Then it collapsed spectacularly when a scandal broke involving sexual relationships with married employees and students, financial mismanagement, and a Wiccan coven called the Blazing Solar Flames. Most Anusara teachers left. He launched a new system called Sridaiva in 2013 that never gained traction.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. His emphasis on bringing scientific framework (acoustics, psychoacoustics, physics of resonance) to the typically mystical sound healing field is well documented.

twoWorlds.notes: The file says he was 'a musician and recording engineer.' Web sources show he was a PUNK ROCK GUITARIST in the Boston scene in the late 1970s, not a 'recording engineer.' He had an epiphany that his rock music was creating disharmony, which led him to study sound healing. He then got a Master's degree from Lesley University. The 'recording engineer' claim appears to be fabricated.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Punk rock guitarist in the late-1970s Boston club scene meets ancient sacred sound traditions (Tibetan, Hindu, indigenous) and the science of psychoacoustics. He had an epiphany that his rock music was contributing to disharmony, pursued a Master's degree from Lesley University studying sound as a healing force, and trained with master sound healers across multiple traditions.

stupidSimplicity.notes: His formula 'Frequency + Intention = Healing' is his most famous contribution and is verified across multiple sources.

remarkableResult.notes: The file says 'Healing Sounds' was 'translated into dozens of languages' — this is plausible but not specifically verified. The book was first published in 1992 (the file says ~1994, which is wrong). World Sound Healing Day since 2002 is verified (February 14th annually). 'Grammy nominee' is verified. 'Simon & Schuster' publisher is verified. The '8 books' claim — S&S shows multiple titles but not necessarily 8. The Sound Healers Association was founded in 1982, which is verified. The 'Visionary Awards' claim is verified (Coalition of Visionary Resources Gold Award).
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Authored 'Healing Sounds' (1992) which became the foundational text of modern sound healing. Grammy-nominated musician. Created the Sound Healers Association (1982) and World Sound Healing Day (observed annually since 2002 on February 14th). His formula 'Frequency + Intention = Healing' became the most widely cited framework in the field. Won the Coalition of Visionary Resources Gold Award.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. She democratized Ashtanga by putting the full series on YouTube, challenging the gatekeeping tradition.

twoWorlds.notes: The file says 'one of the youngest people ever certified' — web sources say she is 'the youngest WOMAN to receive certification.' This is a meaningful distinction. She received certification at age 29. Also, she was certified by Sri K. Pattabhi Jois (not 'the Jois family' as the file implies).
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Social media and digital content creation meets traditional Ashtanga yoga lineage. She was the youngest woman ever certified to teach Ashtanga by Sri K. Pattabhi Jois in Mysore, India, AND became one of the first yoga teachers to build a massive following on Instagram and YouTube, bridging ancient lineage with modern platform culture.

stupidSimplicity.notes: 'Practice and all is coming' is the classic Ashtanga mantra. Her addition of 'but you don't need a guru's permission to start' captures her innovation.

remarkableResult.notes: File says 'over 1 million YouTube subscribers.' Web sources from 2017 show 435K YouTube subs, and later sources say 'over 500,000.' She has over 1 million Instagram followers (not YouTube subscribers). The '140M+ views' YouTube claim from the bio section is not verified in current sources. OmStars platform is verified. '100+ countries' for OmStars students is not verified.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Over 1 million Instagram followers, 500,000+ YouTube subscribers, youngest woman ever certified to teach Ashtanga by Sri K. Pattabhi Jois, author of multiple bestselling yoga books, and built OmStars — the world's first online yoga TV network.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. He did pivot from inspirational content to trauma-informed coaching and publicly acknowledged the limitation of his earlier approach.

twoWorlds.notes: The file says 'he worked in the music business in LA.' This dramatically understates it. He was Senior VP of A&R at Geffen Records by age 21, managed Grammy-winning artists including Gnarls Barkley, and worked at The Firm (management company behind Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Lopez, Korn, Linkin Park). Also, the claim he 'studied with Bessel van der Kolk and Peter Levine' could not be verified — no web sources link Mastin Kipp to direct study with either of them. He may have been influenced by their work but 'studying with' implies direct mentorship.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Major label music executive (youngest Senior VP of A&R at Geffen Records, managed Grammy-winning artists at The Firm) meets clinical trauma science. Went from managing artists like Gnarls Barkley and losing everything to addiction, to sending inspirational emails from a pool house, to building a trauma-informed coaching methodology (Functional Life Coaching) grounded in nervous system regulation.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Good compression of his pivot message.

remarkableResult.notes: Several issues: (1) The Kim Kardashian tweet happened around 2010, not 2012-2013 as the blowUpYear suggests. (2) The file says 'hundreds of thousands of subscribers' for the email list — this is vague but plausible. (3) Book was 'Claim Your Power' by Hay House, confirmed. He also published 'Daily Love: Growing Into Grace' (2014) and 'Reclaim Your Nervous System' (2024) with Hay House. (4) Oprah dubbed him 'up and coming thought leader of the next generation' on Super Soul Sunday, confirmed. (5) Tony Robbins opened a door for him and Louise Hay personally brought him into Hay House — these are additional details that strengthen the result.
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: The Daily Love email list grew massively after a Kim Kardashian tweet drove it from 1,000 to 10,000 followers overnight. Oprah dubbed him 'an up and coming thought leader of the next generation' on Super Soul Sunday and named him to the SuperSoul 100. Published three books with Hay House. He then pivoted to Functional Life Coaching certification, training hundreds of coaches, deliberately trading audience size for depth.

She started Ashtanga at 19 in Costa Rica, studied Anusara alignment, overcame anxiety/depression/eating disorders/addiction. The visual artist detail and Isabelle Moon ethical yogawear are verified. ruleBreak.notes: Verified. His rejection of lifelong medication for ulcerative colitis and his challenge to solemn/clinical breathwork are both well documented.

The '3,000+ certified instructors' is slightly outdated — current sources say 3,500+. The ulcerative colitis healing claim is verified (though 'reversed' and 'cured' are his words; medical establishment would not use these terms).
remarkableResult.suggestedFix: Remove '9D Breathwork' co-creation claim from bio. Result: Reversed his own ulcerative colitis through breathwork and lifestyle changes after being told he'd need medication for life, then built SOMA Breath into a global platform with over 3,500 certified instructors. He is also the lead music producer for the Wim Hof Method.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. His challenge to 'breathe deeply' advice and championing of breathing less/lighter/slower/nasal is his core thesis, well documented.

Web sources say he completed clinical training at the Buteyko Clinic in Moscow and was ACCREDITED by Professor Konstantin Buteyko (in 2002, when Buteyko was still alive — he died in 2003). There is no mention of training under Buteyko's widow. He trained at the clinic and received accreditation from Buteyko himself.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: Buteyko method (Russian clinical breathing science) meets Western sports performance and everyday health. He completed clinical training at the Buteyko Clinic in Moscow and was personally accredited by Dr. Konstantin Buteyko, then translated that clinical methodology into accessible protocols for athletes, asthmatics, and anxious professionals.

remarkableResult.notes: The file says '15+ languages' for the book translation — not specifically verified but plausible. BOLT score as 'industry-standard metric' is well supported. remarkableResult.suggestedFix: 'The Oxygen Advantage' became a global bestseller. His BOLT score became an industry-standard metric used by Olympic athletes and elite sports teams. He has trained over 5,000 people and has certified instructors across 50+ countries through the Oxygen Advantage program.

ruleBreak.notes: Verified. Her teaching about leaning into groundlessness and uncertainty rather than seeking calm is her core message, well documented across many sources.

She was the FIRST American to become a fully ordained nun in the VAJRAYANA tradition (in 1981). This is a more specific and more impressive claim. Also, she had TWO divorces, not just one. Her second divorce is what led her to Buddhism.
twoWorlds.suggestedFix: American elementary school teacher and twice-divorced mother meets Tibetan Buddhist monastic tradition (Shambhala lineage under Chogyam Trungpa). After her second painful divorce in her mid-thirties, she became the first American woman to be fully ordained as a Tibetan Buddhist nun in the Vajrayana tradition (1981), bringing raw emotional honesty and accessible language to dense philosophical teachings.

remarkableResult.suggestedFix: 'When Things Fall Apart' has sold over 1.5 million copies and remained continuously in print for 25+ years. Grew up in a gang from age 11, faced a life-changing moment at 15 when friends were shot in a car ride he narrowly avoided, then had a spiritual awakening and brought that raw, street-forged energy into the transformation space.
